questions.question_text:
A right square pyramid has a surface area of $384\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a base area of $144\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find its perpendicular height, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used the slant height as the perpendicular height without the final Pythagoras step.
Added $10^{2}$ and $6^{2}$ instead of subtracting when finding the perpendicular height.
Doubled the slant height instead of using Pythagoras with half the base edge.

questions.solution_text:
Base edge: $\sqrt{144}=12\text{ cm}$
Area of the four triangles: $384-144=240$
Area of one triangle: $240\div4=60$
Slant height: $60=\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times l$, so $l=10\text{ cm}$
Half the base edge is $6\text{ cm}$.
$h=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=\sqrt{64}=8\text{ cm}$
